pages.text: Mrs. Magpie, who saw everything from the roof, handed Coco a round loaf. "Keep this until evening!" Coco, in a red headscarf, took it in both paws. "Yes! I'll keep it safe on the shelf!"
Coco stood on tiptoe to put it on the highest shelf. But it slipped from their paws and rolled right out the open door. It stopped in the alley dirt, covered in soil.
Coco picked it up. Bits of dirt fell off. "What if she finds out...?" Coco's face felt hot. Coco hid the bread in a corner behind the shelf.
That evening, Mrs. Magpie arrived with a jingle. "Coco, my bread!" Coco's lips stuck shut. "Um... well..." Coco slipped behind the apron of Mom, whose arms were floury.

"Then I'll come tomorrow morning," she said, fluttering up to the roof. Coco took the bread out from behind the shelf and pressed it. Soft that morning, its crust was already hard. Coco's heart felt tight.
Mom sat beside Coco and tapped the hard bread. "Hard as a stone, right?" She held fresh bread beside it. This one was soft! "Saying sorry is like this bread. Before it hardens, say sorry!"
Coco pulled the scarf knot tight with both paws. Holding the dirty bread, Coco went into the alley and looked up at the roof. "Mrs. Magpie! I dropped your bread and got it dirty. I'm sorry!"
She fluttered down from the roof. "Thank you for telling me. I can brush the dirt off!" She brushed the bread with her wing. The tight feeling in Coco's chest became soft and light.

Now, when Coco made a mistake, they did this. "One, don't hide it! Two, right away, before it hardens! Three, look them in the eyes and say it!" The next day, Coco spilled flour and spoke at once. "Mom, I'm sorry!"
Mrs. Magpie patted Coco's back with her wingtip. Hide it, and it hardens. Say it right away, and it softens. Coco looked up at her and smiled. "Before it hardens, say sorry!"
